subject.title: WhatsApp inter_session delivery requests can be wrongly suppressed as REPLY_SKIP / ANNOUNCE_SKIP / NO_REPLY

question: Should this WhatsApp explicit-delivery bug be fixed by landing a narrow message-tool/requester-return-path repair, or by waiting for the broader structured sessions_send handoff contract?
rationale: Both paths change model-facing A2A delivery semantics and overlap an open structured handoff tracker, so automation should not pick the permanent protocol or prompt direction alone.

options.title: Repair the narrow PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the focused fix after addressing its prompt-cache and identifier-redaction blockers, then validate with focused tests and live WhatsApp proof.

options.title: Fold into structured handoff
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader handoff contract explicitly covers delivery intent, skip/no-reply outcomes, and channel/thread inheritance.

options.title: Wait for live repro
options.body: Leave current code unchanged until a fresh WhatsApp repro distinguishes this symptom from legitimate NO_REPLY suppression.

recommendation.title: Repair the narrow PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the focused fix after addressing its prompt-cache and identifier-redaction blockers, then validate with focused tests and live WhatsApp proof.
